newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LATE BHP DIP OVERTURNS RECOVERING AUSTRALIA STOCKS.
newsitem.headline: LATE BHP DIP OVERTURNS RECOVERING AUSTRALIA STOCKS.

text.p: SPI futures 2727.0 -10.0 US 30yr cl 6.53 +0.05
10yrbond futs 93.415 -0.130 Gold NY 321.95 Asia 321.60
AUD US$0.7305 (Thur: $0.7357) CRB Index cl 242.83 +0.02
*Stocks end lower as late BHP tumble overturns a slow recovery from early losses. Volume 374.60 million, A$975.23 million value, 1,107 stocks traded, 356 steady, 391 up, 360 down.
The Australian share market turned weaker again in the last half-hour on Friday as bellwether BHP took a new blow when it announced yet another resignation from senior ranks.
BHP and the main share index had all but recovered from early losses, but the news reversed the trend and the conglomerate's stock ended 45 cents down on the day at A$16.99.

The All Ordinaries index ended 6.3 points down at 2,711.4, while September share price index futures fell 10 to 2,727, a 15.6 point premium to the underlying index. By 4.15 p.m. (0615 GMT) turnover reached A$975 million, with A$159 million in BHP.
BHP has plunged 5.5 percent in two days in reaction to three resignations from the company's senior management, displaying serious conflicts among the conglomerate's leaders.
"This is not looking good. It creates a lot of uncertainty over the future," one senior Sydney-based dealer said.
The third to go was John O'Connor, head of the petroleum division, citing irreconcilable differences between him and the board. The news came just 35 minutes before the market close.
"I'm sure it will take a hit here and overseas tonight, but the underlying assets are good and some people will see it providing ample opportunity to buy," said one BHP analyst.
"The second half should see better throughput and volumes for most of the company's operations," said Prudential-Bache Securities analyst Tony Robson.

There was patchy buying interst in the gold sector as the bullion price improved, and Acacia Resources gained three cents to A$1.43, recovering half of its losses in the wake of Thursday's half-year result.
The banking sector ended 0.24 percent firmer, but stock performance was mixed. Commonwealth Bank rose 25 cents at A$16.82 while National Bank fell three to A$19.63.
"CBA has a reasonable yield by comparison," one dealer said, adding there was no specific news behind the rise.

Transport group Brambles was one of the day's weakest stocks, down 70.8 cents at A$28.40. Dealers said investors took home profits after Thursday's four percent rally to a record A$29.40, sparked by good results from its partner in the Chep pallet business, GKN Plc.

Austrim fell eight cents to A$4.37 in high volume, rumoured to be a sell-off by media enterpreneur Kerry Stokes or packaging magnate Dick Pratt. Brokers said ANZ Securities handled two lines of 9.5 million Austrim shares at A$4.32.

Medical instrument designer Polartechnics was Friday's undisputed winner. It surged 75 cents to a record high of A$4.35 in a much delayed reaction to the June announcement of a strategic alliance with Ethicon Inc to commercialise Polartechnics' cancer detection device, the Polarprobe.
"Finally the penny has dropped. They now realise the importance of the deal," executive chairman Tony Grey told Reuters.
Microscope manufacturer Optiscan Imaging made its debut on the stock exchange at 26 cents, a 30 percent premium to the issue price, before falling back to end at 22 cents.
